name: Dabur India Ltd
title: Dabur India Ltd - 500096 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 India volumes strong (HPC +17%, domestic +9.5%) but RM/PM inflation near 10% forces 4% price hikes; management guides high-single to low-double-digit revenue and margin expansion, with international hit by Middle East.

triggers.label: Inflation ~10%, 4% price hike
triggers.quote: We now see an inflation of roughly around 10% hitting us in a lot of portfolios, barring the portfolio of beverages and healthcare.

triggers.label: FY27 growth raised to high-single to low-double digit
triggers.quote: We are seeing high single to a low double-digit growth because you've got some pricing coming in because of inflation.

triggers.label: HPC grew 17% in Q4
triggers.quote: entire HPC portfolio has grown by 17%

triggers.label: Crude-linked RM ~25%, packaging higher
triggers.quote: crude link bus iness will be 25% from a raw material perspective. If you look packaging material, it could be a little higher.

triggers.label: Middle East ~30-35% of international
triggers.quote: our Middle East business is a good substantial 30%, 3 5% of our overall international business. So that is impacted substantially.

guidance.quote: We are seeing high single to a low double-digit growth because you've got some pricing coming in because of inflation.
At least a double digit is a bare minimum that we expect HPC to grow.
we want to increase the margins from last year to current year.
We expect international business to grow in double digits

red_flags.label: Oral care slowing to 6-7%, market leader regaining
red_flags.quote: oral care being a outlier where we've seen a muted performance of around 6%, 7% growth in Oral Care.

red_flags.label: Glucose down 24-25%, El Nino exposure
red_flags.quote: glucose, which declined by around 24%, 25% for us in the la st quarter

red_flags.label: Margin hit from Middle East alternate supply
red_flags.quote: alternative supply locations, albeit coming at a higher cost and therefore, margin erosion.
